I live along a well known tourist route called the Turquoise Trail running from Santa Fe to Albuquerque so there are a lot of attractions in the area, from museums to historic sites. But there are a few odder or lesser known attractions.

Along the way to Sandia Peak is a funky desert museum called Tinkertown featuring everything from odd collections, mining artifacts, strange dioramas and automata, and even an entire yacht.

http://tinkertown.com/

Nearby is the funky town of Madrid, a relic mining town now home to an eccentric community. It recently drew fame by being featured in the movie Wild Hogs whose fictitious Chile Pepper Festival has now been adopted as a regular event.

http://www.visitmadridnm.com/

New Mexico is one of the US's hot-beds for sustainable architecture and one of its more famous--though not well known to the mainstream culture--is the Earthship community in Taos, north of Santa Fe. Earthships are based on rammed earth and tire construction covered in adobe and are known for their high degree of built-in self-sufficiency through the use of an indoor garden. The Earthship community has often been controversial due to the mercurial attitudes of government authorities toward green building.

http://earthship.com/

People in New Mexico often seem to develop a special connection to the earth--something that goes back to its ancient history of Pueblos and cliff dwellings. But in modern times this has developed in various other ways. In Farmington NM a geologist became enamoured of a particular cliffside location and decided to apply a friend's skills with explosives to the creation of a unique excavated cliff dwelling that long served as his personal office. Today it is available as a small bed & breakfast named Kokopelli's Cave.

http://kokoscave.com/

In an area called Los Nidos, between Taos and Santa Fe, artist Ra Paulette has spent decades hand-carving the natural sandstone into a vast series of free-form-organic-designed complexes of amazing beauty. His goal is to create a unique resort retreat. Once obscure, it has recently started to be discovered by tourists thanks to being featured in a documentary, but is still relatively unknown. Two of his astounding creations are currently for sale.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oxcftjJ39BU

http://www.racavedigger.com/racavedigger.com/Ra_Paulette_Home.html

A little farther north in Los Alamos is a place legendary among hardcore tech nerds but few others, the Black Hole Surplus shop, formerly known as the Los Alamos Sales Company. Created by a former Los Alamos Labs machinist, the shop featured some of the rarest of defense department surplus hardware right from the famous nuclear research facility. The shop was closed for some time but the web site claims it is currently open, though operating hours seem uncertain.

http://www.blackholesurplus.com/

Going back to Santa Fe there's another site also legendary to true nerds but unknown to the general public--the El Farol Bar. The El Farol is famous among math nerds because it has leant its name to one of the key theoretical problems of game theory.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Farol_Bar_problem

I've considered the place as a location for Science Pub events, but locals don't seem too interested in such things.

http://www.elfarolsf.com/

This fall Santa Fe will become home to a very new and unique attraction called Meow Wolf. The project of a local installation art collective, Meow Wolf recently received help from Game of Thrones author with the purchase of an abandoned bowling alley on the west side of town. This space will soon house a mind-blowing exhibit known as the House of Eternal Return.

http://meowwolf.com/art-complex/

If you continue past Meramec Caverns State Park, about 10min further up on the left, there's this teeny, family-owned reptile house petting zoo. They let you hold the tamer animals (as long as your gentle, etc) and interact with just about all of them (except the giant alligator, who was a rescue animal and less friendly), and for a $3 additional fee, you can pet/etc the LION they have around back in a roomy fenced enclosure. I went from being annoyed that the caverns didn't meet my needs (another story altogether) to being up close and even licked by an actual, factual, fully grown (friendly) lion. It made my whole summer.
